decisions.summary: C15 (drop onto a guard, 1 m) and C16 (wall hit, 3 m/s) are judged in the strong filament (nylon-CF, strong_material) by CalculiX on the free drone, an elastic floor. params.name: topo_prop_cost

The extra (topo_prop_cost - 1) is divided by the number of designable cells in that cell's column, filled or not (topopt3d.regions), so every cell under a prop costs a flat 1.53-1.60 on the 1.33 mm grid (1.82-2.0 on the 2 mm grid). That is a charge per volume, not one shadow per column: a wide flange and a deep web of the same volume pay the same, though the flange casts more shadow, and the charge changes with topo_h and topo_below (topopt3d: known limitations). Swept at 2 mm: 3 drew 22 % shadow, 8 drew 15.9 %, 16 drew 11.8 %, 30 drew 8.5 % at 2.9x the compliance. 10 was chosen for C14's 15 %. The sweep does not carry over to the 1.33 mm grid as it is, and C14 judges the drawn frame's real shadow.

params.name: topo_thrust_factor
params.rationale: Thrust load on a seat, x full static thrust: a hard throttle punch.

params.name: topo_crash_n
params.rationale: N, the crash load on a hoop for the optimiser (a magnitude only scales its compliance; the CalculiX crash check uses the real impact energy).

params.name: topo_battery_g
params.rationale: g of deceleration on the battery, hanging on the strap, in a crash.

params.name: topo_crash_spread_deg
params.rationale: deg either side of the guard arc's middle where it is also hit: the crashes land across the whole arc, not at one point.

params.name: topo_w_battery
params.rationale: Weights of the load cases in the objective (each compliance normalised by its start). Crashes weigh as much as the flight load: a 10-year-old's drone is mostly a crash-test article (the review: 'it will break after a couple of crashes'). Thrust at 2 and the two prop strikes (topo_w_strike) hold the motor seats: the first run, with thrust at 1 and no strikes, tied the hoops to the posts and left the seats on grey threads. The strikes push the seat in its own plane only; the tilt a strike at the prop plane also puts on it is not modelled (topopt3d: known limitations). The crashes come from many directions: straight in (topo_w_crash) and in-and-up from below (topo_w_crash_up) at the arc's middle and both ends, along the arc (topo_w_crash_t), up from below (topo_w_vertical), down from above (topo_w_top). In-plane hits at two points alone drew straight bars.

params.name: topo_patch_mm
params.rationale: mm, radius of the patch of hoop a crash load lands on.

params.name: surface_edge_mm
params.rationale: mm, the level set's edge length. 0.4 lost: 2x the triangles, no visible change.

params.name: surface_blur_mm
params.rationale: mm, Gaussian blur on the resampled field: rounds the field's cells' creases. 0.7 lost: on a limb one cell thick (the thin flanges the optimiser puts in the grid's floor, the diagonal staircases) it pulled the density under the surface and erased the limb, leaving stubs; CalculiX found the drawn seat 12x softer than the optimiser's own model (1.25 against 15.3 N/mm). At 0.35 the two agree (15.7 N/mm). 0 lost too: diagonal joints parted (0.41 N/mm).

params.name: surface_iso
params.rationale: Density at the surface: the volume-preserving level, where the limbs drawn hold the volume the optimiser placed (measured on the first 2 mm field, the sum of rho 6237 mm^3 against ~6200 drawn at 0.36). 0.5 lost: that field's thinnest members sat at 0.7-0.9 density behind the 5 mm filter, and 0.5 drew half its volume, in 9 pieces.

params.name: surface_scale_mm
params.rationale: mm per unit density: turns the blurred field into a distance for the fillet blend.

params.name: surface_fillet_mm
params.rationale: mm, smooth-union radius where a limb meets a seat, hoop or post: the fillet.

params.name: surface_simplify_mm
params.rationale: mm, mesh simplification tolerance (faces move less than this): enough to remove the level set's zero-length edges and nothing else. 0.02 lost: it let a long triangle from a fillet's rim span a seat 0.012 mm proud of its top, into the motor (C5 read 0.0175 mm^3).

params.name: surface_open_mm
params.rationale: mm, radius of the morphological opening of the drawn frame (geometry._open): any part thinner than about twice this goes. Half of cad.wall_thickness's 1.26 mm (perimeters x extrusion_width_mm) and a hair over, so it leaves no section under that: change it with either. Every section it would take is first grown where it can (geometry._thicken), so it takes what could not grow: the feathered edges, down to 0.01 mm, where the field met a keep-out at a grazing angle, the lips a cut leaves, and sections cut on both faces (the hub, 1.4 mm between two cuts, is spared). 0.3, opening before any thickening, left the rim's 0.35 mm sheets (C7). 0.63 lost when nothing was thickened first: it also deleted the rim's four bridges between neighbouring guards that the optimiser drew, and left the arcs ending in stubs (the author's 'nubs', 2026-10-17). 0.75 lost on a 2 mm field: it broke the frame apart.

params.name: surface_cut_round_mm
params.rationale: mm, the radius every keep-out's edges are rounded to (geometry._keepout_sdf), so a cut leaves the frame a fillet where it meets the body, as a 0.4 mm nozzle prints it. Sharp, those re-entrant edges were stress singularities the crash checks' peak sat on, growing with every mesh refinement.

params.name: surface_clearance_mm
params.rationale: mm the drawn field stands off every keep-out: the level set interpolates the cut linearly and the simplification moves faces, each by hundredths of a millimetre, and the fit check counts any overlap past 1e-4 mm^3 (C5). Not on the hub's two faces: there the battery's and the strap's keep-outs end this far below z = 0 and the board's start this far above hub_t, so the hub is hub_t thick (geometry._keepout_sdf); a plane's level set is exact, so the fit check finds no overlap on them.

params.name: print_tilt_deg
params.rationale: deg the frame is tilted on the bed from flying-level, about the horizontal axis at print_azimuth_deg. The layers lie square to the build direction, so this sets which way the printed part is weak (fea.layer_normal). Flat, as it flies: the orientation scan on CalculiX's crash stresses found that flat loses no strength to the layers (tilts of 75-105 deg lose up to 14 % at some headings), and flat stands 20 mm tall with support under 22 % of its surface. On edge (90-105 deg) lost: 10 % support, but 111 mm tall on its rim, five times the layers.

params.name: print_azimuth_deg
params.rationale: deg, the tilt axis's direction from +x (forward).

params.name: support_area_max_frac
params.rationale: Share of the frame's surface the slicer may support (downward faces past 45 deg, fdm.overhang). R7 allows supports; past about a third of the surface the print is mostly support to peel, and every supported face is a scar.

params.name: bed_x_mm
params.rationale: mm, Snapmaker U1 build plate X (Snapmaker specs: 270 mm cube).

params.name: bed_y_mm
params.rationale: mm, Snapmaker U1 build plate Y.

params.name: bed_z_mm
params.rationale: Snapmaker U1 build height.

params.name: brim_mm
params.rationale: mm of brim per side; snipped off.

params.name: nozzle_d_mm
params.rationale: mm, the U1's stock nozzle.

params.name: extrusion_width_mm
params.rationale: mm, 1.05 x nozzle - a stock profile's line width; 3 of them is the wall rule.

params.name: layer_height_mm
params.rationale: mm, 0.2: half the nozzle, the PETG default.

params.name: perimeters
params.rationale: Wall loops.

params.name: infill_fraction
params.rationale: The limbs are a few mm across: treat as solid.

params.name: print_speed_mm_s
params.rationale: mm/s nominal; an ordinary PETG speed (the estimate derates it).

params.name: max_print_time_h
params.rationale: An afternoon with a 10-year-old: a print that runs overnight is a print he does not see.

params.name: max_filament_g
params.rationale: g, one spool.

params.name: guard_thrust_factor
params.rationale: Static thrust with the guards and the limbs under the props, relative to the open-prop bench test. ASSUMPTION (A1): low guards neither add (no duct lip) nor take much; the limbs' shadow on the disc is capped at 15 % by claim C14, and blockage costs roughly half its area fraction.

params.name: usable_capacity_frac
params.rationale: Land at ~3.5 V/cell: 80% of rated capacity, kinder to cheap 1S packs.

params.name: prop_sweep_half_h
params.rationale: mm, half-height of the band the prop occupies, for the clearance checks.

params.name: fea_mesh_mm
params.rationale: mm, the CalculiX tetrahedra's edge (quadratic tets, two to three across a 3-4 mm limb); solid_fea_ccx refuses a mesh with tets over 2x this or slivers. petgasus.fea_converged reruns on the fine surface with tets to 0.75 of it, and refuses a first mode that moves more than 5 % or a drop height or wall speed that moves more than 10 %. 1.2 lost: fTetWild's mesh of it held ~200k tets, and the fine one at 0.9 mm ~2M unknowns, too many for the single- threaded equation solver (solid_fea_ccx.run) on a 21 GB machine.

params.name: fea_surface_mm
params.rationale: mm, edge of the analysis surface (geometry.analysis_surface: the frame as one signed function and one level set, no booleans); the convergence check's fine surface is 0.7 of it. 0.5, the printed surface's own edge: CalculiX judges the very surface that is printed. 0.8 lost: on its coarser lattice a rim bridge's 1.2 mm neck thinned to a thread (genus 47 against the print's 50), the tet mesh cut it, and the frame had a loose piece (a 0 Hz mode, a solve 434 N out of equilibrium). The printed surface simplified to 0.1 mm lost: the booleans' cut lines left slivers gmsh could not recover a boundary from, and simplifying them made the surface intersect itself.

blocked.hint: an evaluator skipped — its tool is missing here, it skipped itself on its input, or a prerequisite is not established — and none failed: no usable verdict

errored.hint: an evaluator errored: it crashed, so nothing was evaluated, and the evaluator itself is broken

fail.hint: an evaluator failed the current design, a physical result failed, or an evaluator's value does not meet the claim's acceptance condition

pass.hint: every evaluator is qualified and passed on the current inputs, inside its operating context, and every value compared with the acceptance condition meets it — checked does not mean true

pending.hint: an evaluator of the claim is unrun on the current inputs

refuted.hint: an evaluator failed the current design, a physical result failed, or an evaluator's value does not meet the claim's acceptance condition

stale.hint: a pass whose read set has changed since, or whose prerequisite is invalidated or unrun: nothing is checked now

unclaimed.hint: no evaluator, none qualified, one unqualified, or one outside its operating context; or an assumption nobody owns

unverified.hint: waits on an article: no physical result yet, or a pass no article binds to the current inputs

verified.hint: every evaluator is qualified and passed on the current inputs, inside its operating context, and every value compared with the acceptance condition meets it — checked does not mean true
